title: continuous-batcher: scheduler tuning for queueing, fairness, starvation prevention, and timeouts
author: Aisha Kapoor
description: Motivation: production workloads have shown occasional starvation for low-priority short requests during high-throughput tails. This PR tunes the continuous-batcher scheduler to improve queueing fairness, add starvation prevention, and make timeouts explicit and configurable. Summary of changes: 1) Introduce per-queue max_wait_ms and a lightweight priority aging (age_boost_coef) that increases effective priority for items waiting longer than a threshold. 2) Add a soft timeout path that promotes queued requests past a configurable wait boundary to avoid indefinite starvation; requests still respect downstream execution timeouts. 3) Improve fairness by switching from strict round-robin to a hybrid deficit-based scheme with configurable quantum and aging. 4) Expose new metrics (queue_wait_seconds_bucket, queue_promoted_total, queue_starved_count) and hooks for tracing request lifecycle. 5) Add unit and integration tests for corner cases (priority inversion, concurrent promotions) and a perf benchmark harness to verify overhead. Checklist: - [x] Design doc attached in comments - [x] Unit tests added - [x] Integration tests added - [x] Benchmarks run against prod-like traces - [x] Docs/runbook updated Impact: On internal perf traces (mix of short chat completions and long generation) we observed: - median latency: +1% (negligible) - p95 latency for short requests: -12% - p99 tail wait time reduced by ~28% - throughput at 95th percentile maintained within 3% of baseline Safety: All behavior is behind config flags and runtime feature gate (continuous_batcher.force_new_scheduler=false by default). Rolling rollout recommended: enable on a small subset of Dedicated pools first, monitor queue_promoted_total and queue_starved_count. Migration notes: existing configs are backward compatible; new parameters are optional. See docs/runbooks/continuous-batcher-tuning.md for recommended settings and observability queries.

review_comments: Liam Chen (2025-11-14): Can you clarify the complexity of the promotion path? Does it add any lock contention on the hot path?

Aisha Kapoor (2025-11-14): The promotion happens only on the enqueue/dequeue boundaries and uses an atomic age counter per queue; no global locks added. I ran a contention profile in perf/bench showing <1% overhead in the hot path.
Priya Nair (2025-11-16): We need an explicit config for maximum promotions per-second to avoid promotion storms on bursty workloads.
Aisha Kapoor (2025-11-16): Added max_promotions_per_sec with a default conservative value and added tests that simulate bursty arrivals (see scheduler_test.cc).
Jordan Matthews (2025-11-18): Approving after minor nit on metric naming; suggest queue_promoted_total to match existing Prometheus conventions.
Aisha Kapoor (2025-11-18): Renamed metric to queue_promoted_total and updated dashboards in docs/runbooks. CI greened after metric rename.
testing_summary: Unit tests (scheduler_test) cover priority aging, promotion, and timeout paths. Integration test runs on canary Dedicated pool with mixed load trace reproduced in perf/bench. CI: lint, unit, integration, and e2e perf checks. Benchmarks run against 3 workload profiles; results attached in perf/bench/bench_results.md.
perf_results: Profiled with 1000 clients: p99 wait time reduced 28%, short-request p95 latency reduced 12%, overall throughput within 3% of baseline. Overhead of scheduler: ~0.5% CPU increase under steady state.

release_notes: Improved fairness and starvation prevention in continuous-batcher scheduler. New runtime configs: max_wait_ms, age_boost_coef, max_promotions_per_sec, scheduler_quantum_ms. Backwards compatible and gated behind feature flag.
